$comment: v3, 22 October 2026, Option B: rccat carries content and time eligibility only. User-state eligibility (account, age, opt-out, register) is implied by the wagering deal, with legal bases and policy reference recorded in the deal terms or the Deals API.
title: Restricted Category Eligibility (rccat): proposed OpenRTB community extension
description: Seller-certified, impression-level content and time eligibility for restricted ad categories. First use case: Australian wagering advertising (Interactive Gambling Act 2001, Part 7C). Validates the imp.ext object. rccat carries no user IDs, user.id, eids, IFAs, age, login state, opt-out status or register status, and no per-person eligibility signal. User-state eligibility travels with the deal; user-state ineligibility is never signalled and shows only as the absence of a wagering deal. Use limit: receivers use rccat and deal presence only for the bid decision and compliance audit logs. They must not store either against user or device identifiers; use either for targeting, segmentation, frequency capping or measurement; infer restricted-user status from the presence or absence of a wagering deal or an attestation; or retain either beyond its purpose and the applicable retention period. bcat always wins over rccat.

rccat.description: Restricted-category eligibility container at imp.ext.rccat. Impression level, because eligibility can change with user state, event phase and playout time.

elig.description: One entry per restricted category the seller has evaluated for this impression. No entry for a category means the seller hasn't attested eligibility for it; treat as not eligible.

cattax.description: Taxonomy for cat, from AdCOM List: Category Taxonomies. 8 = Ad Product Taxonomy 2.0. 3 = Ad Product Taxonomy 1.0 for legacy partners. Content taxonomies aren't valid here: this describes the advertised product, not the content.

cat.description: Most specific advertised-product category IDs evaluated. An attestation covers the stated ID and its children, never its parents or siblings. In Ad Product Taxonomy 2.0: 1361 Gambling, 1362 Casinos, 1363 Contests, 1364 Give Aways, 1365 Lottery, 1366 Sports Betting, 1367 Virtual Betting. For Australian licensed wagering, attest on 1366; 1361 would also cover products that can't lawfully be offered.

eligible.description: 1 = eligible on content and time grounds: the seller's controls for every basis listed have passed. 0 = blocked on content or time grounds that are the same for every viewer, such as a live sport window measured in the viewer's legal local time. Never used for user state, which travels with the deal.

deal_only.description: Applies when eligible = 1. 1 = eligible only through the deal IDs in imp.pmp.deals; with no deal, treat as not eligible. 0 = eligible in any auction on this impression, including the open exchange. Use 0 only where the regime has no user-level rules, because user checks travel with the deal. Australian wagering is always 1.

basis.description: Content and time bases evaluated, as jurisdiction-regime-provision codes. Australian codes: au-iga-62r (live sport, 5:00 am to 8:30 pm), au-iga-62ra (live sport, 8:30 pm to 5:00 am), au-iga-62ua (BVOD and SVOD programs directed towards children) and au-iga-62ub (G, C or P programs at set times on BVOD and SVOD). See the Basis codes table in rccat.md. User-state bases such as au-iga-62p and au-iga-62q belong in the deal terms, not here.

policy.description: Seller control-set or policy-version reference, for audit. Never identifies a user.

checked_at.description: UTC time the seller made this impression's eligibility decision. Never the date of an individual's age check or register lookup.
